subject.summary: The Khyber Pass between Jamrud and Torkham: measured terrain from NASA SRTM elevation, the road that carries the pass, and the four places that mark it. The relief is true to the data at 1:2 560; heights are exaggerated 1.35x for reading.

sources.title: The user's request
sources.ref: A film of the Khyber Pass for a vertical 9:16 film, assembling across a piece of music.

sources.title: NASA SRTM 30 m (SRTMGL1)
sources.ref: https://portal.opentopography.org/raster?opentopoID=OTSRTM.082015.4326.1 - sampled at 0.004 deg (~370 m) over 71.014-71.458 E, 33.954-34.168 N

sources.title: OpenStreetMap road geometry (ODbL)
sources.ref: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright - the N-5/AH1 road from Jamrud (34.0000, 71.3833) to Torkham (34.1217, 71.1031), 914 geometry points, measured 38.3 km

sources.title: Khyber Pass - Wikipedia
sources.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khyber_Pass - pass proper 40 km Jamrud to Landi Kotal, 13 km more to Loya Daka, 460 m descent to the Peshawar valley, Khyber Pass Railway opened 1925.

sources.title: Ali Masjid - Wikipedia
sources.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Masjid - the narrowest point of the pass, elevation 967 m (3,174 ft), 16 km east of Landi Kotal.

sources.title: Landi Kotal - Wikipedia
sources.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landi_Kotal - 1,072 m above sea level; the western edge of the pass, 5 km from Afghanistan.

sources.title: Torkham - Wikipedia
sources.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torkham - the border crossing 5 km west of the summit of the pass.

sources.title: Jamrud Fort - Wikipedia
sources.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamrud_Fort - foundation laid by Hari Singh Nalwa on 18 December 1836, completed in 54 days, walls 10 ft (3 m) thick, originally named Fatehgarh.

sources.title: Bab-e-Khyber - Wikipedia
sources.ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bab-e-Khyber - the Khyber Gate at the entrance of the pass, beside Jamrud Fort; inaugurated by Field Marshal Ayub Khan on 11 June 1963.

parts.label: Terrain
parts.note: Sampled from NASA SRTM 30 m elevation on a 68 x 39 grid; contours every 50 m, index contours every 250 m. Rotated a quarter turn so the pass runs up the tall frame.

parts.label: High point
parts.note: The highest ground in the measured area, north of the pass; not a named summit.

parts.label: Khyber Pass road
parts.note: The road from Jamrud to Torkham, draped on the terrain: 38.3 km of the OpenStreetMap geometry.

parts.label: Jamrud Fort
parts.note: The eastern entrance to the pass, beside the Bab-e-Khyber gate. Its fort was laid out by Hari Singh Nalwa on 18 December 1836 and finished in 54 days, with walls 10 ft (3 m) thick. Position 34.0000, 71.3833.

parts.label: Ali Masjid
parts.note: The narrowest point of the pass, 967 m above sea level, named for the mosque beside the road. Position 34.0290, 71.2620.

parts.label: Landi Kotal
parts.note: The summit town, 1,072 m above sea level, and the terminus the Khyber Pass Railway reached in 1925. Position 34.1053, 71.1553.

parts.label: Torkham
parts.note: The border crossing with Afghanistan, 5 km west of the summit. Position 34.1217, 71.1031.

parts.label: Bab-e-Khyber
parts.note: The Khyber Gate, at the entrance of the pass beside Jamrud Fort; inaugurated on 11 June 1963. Position 34.0025, 71.3800.
